問題: One child, one teacher, one textbook and one pen can change the world. Education is the only solution.
訳: 一人の子ども、一人の教師、一冊の教科書、そして一本のペンが世界を変えられる。教育こそが唯一の解決策なのだ。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentences above?
問題01選択肢A: Only when many children and teachers come together with lots of books and pens can the world be changed, and education is just one of several solutions.
問題01選択肢B: A single child or teacher may change the world, but education by itself is not enough to solve our problems.
問題01選択肢C: A pen can change the world far more than education can, so the pen is the only solution we really need.
問題01選択肢D: Even one child, one teacher, one book, or one pen has the power to change the world, and education is the one and only way to solve our problems.
問題01の解説: 元の文は「一つ一つの小さな力でも世界を変えられる」「教育こそ唯一の解決策」という二点なので、その両方を言い換えたDが正解。Aは「one」を「many」に、「only solution」を「one of several」に変えて数量と唯一性を崩している。Bは「教育だけでは足りない」と本文の only solution に真っ向から矛盾し、Cは本文にないペンと教育の優劣比較を持ち込んでいるため、いずれも意味がずれる。

問題: I gave some presents to my sisters, and they gave me a very nice present back.
訳: 私は姉妹にプレゼントをいくつかあげ、彼女たちはお返しにとても素敵なプレゼントをくれた。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: My sisters received a few gifts from me, and in return they gave me one wonderful gift.
問題01選択肢B: My sisters gave me several presents, and I gave them a lovely one in return.
問題01選択肢C: I handed my sisters just one present, and they returned several wonderful gifts to me.
問題01選択肢D: I gave my sisters a few presents, but they gave nothing back to me.
問題01の解説: 元の文は「私が姉妹に複数のプレゼントをあげ、彼女たちが私に一つの素敵なプレゼントをくれた」という意味。贈る向きと数量が一致するAが正解(received a few gifts from me = 私が複数あげた、they gave me one = 一つくれた)。Bは贈り手と受け手が逆。Cは数量が逆(私が一つ贈り、複数もらう)。Dはお返しをもらった事実(gave me a present back)を否定しており意味がずれる。

問題: All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.
訳: 勉強ばかりで遊ばないと、ジャックはつまらない子になる。（よく学び、よく遊べ。）
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentence above (All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.)?
問題01選択肢A: Jack is a dull boy, so he keeps working hard and never finds time to play.
問題01選択肢B: Because Jack both works hard and plays a lot, he grows into a lively and interesting boy.
問題01選択肢C: If Jack does nothing but work and never takes time to play, he becomes a boring person.
問題01選択肢D: If Jack only plays and never does any work, he ends up as a boring person.
問題01の解説: 元の文は「働くばかりで遊ばないこと」が原因で Jack が退屈になる、という因果を表すのでCが最も同義。Aは原因と結果を逆にして「もともと退屈だから働く」としており、Bは結果を正反対のプラスにしており、Dは work と play を入れ替えているため、いずれも意味がずれる。

問題: You cannot learn about your dog's health from his nose. A better way is to look at his gums.
訳: 犬の健康状態は、鼻からはわからない。より良い方法は、歯茎を見ることだ。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentences above?
問題01選択肢A: Your dog's nose shows its health more clearly than its gums do.
問題01選択肢B: Checking your dog's gums tells you more about its health than checking its nose does.
問題01選択肢C: Neither your dog's nose nor its gums can tell you how healthy your dog is.
問題01選択肢D: To keep your dog healthy, you should clean its nose instead of its gums.
問題01の解説: 原文は『鼻では健康はわからず、歯茎を見るほうがよい』という内容なので、歯茎のほうが多くわかるとするBが同義です。Aは鼻と歯茎の優劣が逆、Cは歯茎も役立たないと言い切る点で本文と矛盾し、Dは『健康を知る方法』ではなく『鼻を掃除して健康に保つ』という別の話にすり替わっています。

問題: The first GPS satellite was sent into space in 1978 and seven years later eleven satellites were flying around the earth.
訳: 最初のGPS衛星は1978年に宇宙へ打ち上げられ、その7年後には11基の衛星が地球の周りを飛んでいた。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: The first GPS satellite went into space in 1978, and by 1985 eleven satellites were circling the earth.
問題01選択肢B: The first GPS satellite went into space in 1978, and seven years earlier eleven satellites were already circling the earth.
問題01選択肢C: In 1978 eleven GPS satellites were launched together, and the first of them started circling the earth seven years later.
問題01選択肢D: The first GPS satellite went into space in 1978, and seven years later only seven satellites were circling the earth.
問題01の解説: 1978年から7年後は1985年なので、by 1985 eleven satellites were circling とするAが原文と同じ意味になる。Bは『seven years earlier(7年前)』として時間の向きを逆にしており誤り。Cは1978年に11基を打ち上げたことにしていて本文と数・順序が合わない。Dはeleven(11基)をseven(7基)に変えており数量がずれるので不適切。

問題: Richard and Elizabeth came to Kiyoyama by train and bus from Tokyo to experience real Japanese culture. Their first difficulty was at reception. After five minutes of trying to understand their names, the young receptionist gave up and went into a back office.
訳: リチャードとエリザベスは、本物の日本文化を体験するために、東京から電車とバスでキヨヤマへやって来た。最初の困難は受付でのことだった。5分間、二人の名前を聞き取ろうとした末に、若い受付係はあきらめて奥の事務室へ入っていった。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the underlined sentence: "After five minutes of trying to understand their names, the young receptionist gave up and went into a back office"?
問題01選択肢A: The young receptionist could not catch the guests' names in five minutes, so she gave up and went to a back room.
問題01選択肢B: The young receptionist caught the two guests' names in five minutes and then showed them to a back room.
問題01選択肢C: After five minutes of trying to say the receptionist's name, the two guests gave up and went to a back room.
問題01選択肢D: The young receptionist asked the guests to wait and went to a back room to look for their names.
問題01の解説: 元の文は『5分間、二人の名前を聞き取ろうとしたが、受付係はあきらめて奥へ行った』という意味。聞き取れずにあきらめて奥へ行った、とするAが同義で正解。Bは『聞き取れて案内した』とし gave up と矛盾。Cは主語を the two guests にし、聞き取る対象も『受付係の名前』に取り違えている。Dは『名前を探しに奥へ行った』という本文にない行動にすり替えており、いずれも意味がずれる。

問題: There are different kinds of World Heritage Sites. Some places have natural beauty and other places have important histories.
訳: 世界遺産にはさまざまな種類がある。自然の美しさを持つ場所もあれば、重要な歴史を持つ場所もある。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentences above?
問題01選択肢A: Every World Heritage Site is famous for both its beautiful scenery and its long history.
問題01選択肢B: World Heritage Sites come in several types; some places are known for their beautiful nature, and others for their important past.
問題01選択肢C: A place can become a World Heritage Site only when it has both natural beauty and an important history.
問題01選択肢D: World Heritage Sites matter because of their natural beauty, not because of their history.
問題01の解説: 原文は「種類はさまざまで、自然の美しい場所もあれば、重要な歴史の場所もある」なので、kinds/types・natural beauty/beautiful nature・histories/past と言い換えたBが同義。AとCは Some ... other ... が別々の場所を指すのに「どの遺産も両方(both)」「両方を持つときだけ(only when)」と両立させており意味がずれる。Dは歴史を理由から外して(not ... history)おり、歴史的な場所も含む原文と明確に矛盾する。

問題: Pet owners should think about the environment such as parks, streets, mountains and rivers, and should not damage it.
訳: ペットの飼い主は、公園、道路、山、川といった環境のことを考え、それを傷つけてはならない。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: People who keep pets ought to care about places such as parks and rivers, but it is fine for them to harm those places.
問題01選択肢B: The environment, such as parks and rivers, should take care of the pets that people keep.
問題01選択肢C: People who keep pets ought to care about places such as parks and rivers, and they must not harm them.
問題01選択肢D: People who keep pets only need to protect rivers and mountains, not parks or streets.
問題01の解説: 元の文は『飼い主は環境のことを考え、それを傷つけてはならない』という意味。care about places such as parks and rivers, and must not harm them と言い換えたCが正解。Aは前半は合うが『傷つけても構わない(it is fine to harm)』が should not damage と正反対。Bは環境が飼い主(のペット)の世話をするという主客の逆転。Dは parks や streets を除外しており『すべてを含む例示』の本文と食い違う。よってC以外は意味が明確にずれる。

問題: There was a time when women social activists asked men to fight for women's rights. But this time, we will do it by ourselves. I'm not telling men to stop speaking for women's rights.
訳: かつて、女性の社会活動家が、女性の権利のために闘ってくれるよう男性に頼んだ時代があった。しかし今回は、私たちが自分たちの手でそれを行う。男性に、女性の権利のために発言するのをやめてほしいと言っているのではない。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentences above?
問題01選択肢A: In the past, women activists asked men to fight for women's rights, but this time women will do it themselves; still, the speaker is not asking men to stop speaking up for those rights.
問題01選択肢B: In the past, women activists asked men to fight for women's rights, and this time too they will leave the fight to men, hoping men keep speaking up for those rights.
問題01選択肢C: In the past, women activists asked men to fight for women's rights, but this time women will do it themselves, and now the speaker wants men to stop speaking up for those rights.
問題01選択肢D: In the past, women fought for their rights by themselves, but this time they will ask men to fight for them and to speak up for those rights.
問題01の解説: 元の文は『以前は男性に頼んだ→今回は女性自身で行う→でも男性に発言をやめてほしいわけではない』。Aだけがこの3点を正しく言い換えているので正解。Bは this time too ... leave the fight to men として But this time, we will do it by ourselves と矛盾。Cは A と最後の節だけが異なり、wants men to stop speaking up と I'm not telling men to stop の否定を逆にしている。Dは冒頭で『以前は女性が自分たちで闘った』『今回は男性に頼む』と過去と現在・動作主を入れ替えているため誤り。

問題: It is tough to live in Antarctica for a number of reasons. The biggest problem is that Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth, and about 98% is covered in ice.
訳: 南極大陸で暮らすのが厳しいのには、いくつもの理由がある。最大の問題は、南極が地球上で最も寒い場所であり、その約98％が氷に覆われていることだ。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentences above?
問題01選択肢A: Living in Antarctica is hard for just one reason: it is the coldest place on Earth, and about 98% of it is covered in ice.
問題01選択肢B: Living in Antarctica is hard for several reasons, and the worst is that it is one of the coldest places on Earth and nearly all of it lies under ice.
問題01選択肢C: There are several reasons why Antarctica is easy to live in, the main one being that it is the coldest place on Earth with about 98% under ice.
問題01選択肢D: Living in Antarctica is hard for several reasons, the most serious being that no place on Earth is colder and almost all of it is buried under ice.
問題01の解説: 原文は『いくつもの理由』『最も寒い場所』『約98％が氷』を述べており、Dは別の語（no place on Earth is colder＝最も寒い、almost all＝ほぼ全部が氷の下）で正しく言い換えているので同義。Aは理由を『just one reason（ただ一つ）』に限定している点でずれる。Bは『one of the coldest places（最も寒い場所の一つ）』と最上級の意味を弱めている点でずれる。Cはhard（厳しい）をeasy（暮らしやすい）に反転させており意味が逆になる。

問題: In 1863, people from schools and clubs all over England met in a pub in London. They wanted to agree on the rules of football. For example, should running with the ball in their hands be allowed? After a lot of talking, the men who wanted to say yes to such a question walked out. They wanted to play rugby football.
訳: 1863年、イングランド中の学校やクラブの人々がロンドンのパブに集まった。彼らはフットボールのルールについて合意したかったのだ。たとえば、ボールを手に持って走ることは認められるべきか。長い議論の末、そうした問いにイエスと言いたい男たちは席を立って出て行った。彼らはラグビーフットボールをやりたかったのである。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the passage above?
問題01選択肢A: The people who believed players should not be allowed to carry the ball by hand walked out and went off to play rugby.
問題01選択肢B: After a long discussion, everyone at the meeting finally agreed that carrying the ball by hand should be allowed.
問題01選択肢C: The people who believed players should be allowed to carry the ball by hand left the meeting because they wanted to play rugby.
問題01選択肢D: The people who wanted to carry the ball by hand stayed at the meeting, while the others left to play rugby.
問題01の解説: 本文の『イエスと言いたい（＝手で運ぶことを認めたい）男たちが出て行き、ラグビーをやりたかった』を言い換えたCが正解。Aは should not be allowed と否定が逆。Bは実際には一部が退席して合意していないので矛盾。Dは残った人と出て行った人が入れ替わっており、認めたい人こそが退席した本文と食い違う。

問題: It was not until the discovery of the Rosetta Stone that some clues to the Egyptian language became known.
訳: ロゼッタストーンが発見されて初めて、エジプトの言語を解く手がかりがいくらか知られるようになった。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: People learned some clues to the Egyptian language long before the Rosetta Stone was found.
問題01選択肢B: People did not find any clues to the Egyptian language until the Rosetta Stone was discovered.
問題01選択肢C: The Rosetta Stone was discovered because people had already found some clues to the Egyptian language.
問題01選択肢D: Even after the Rosetta Stone was discovered, clues to the Egyptian language stayed unknown.
問題01の解説: 元の文は『ロゼッタストーンが見つかるまでは手がかりは知られなかった＝見つかって初めて知られた』という意味なので、「見つかるまで手がかりは得られなかった」と言い換えたBが同義。Aは発見よりずっと前に手がかりがあったとして時間を逆にし、Cは手がかりが先で発見が後だと因果を逆にし、Dは発見後も手がかりが不明のままだとして本文の結論を否定しているため、いずれも意味が明確にずれている。

問題: Today Jane is eighty, but she still travels almost 300 days a year. She talks to people about the power they have to help other people, animals and the environment. Some day you may have a chance to meet and talk to her.
訳: 現在ジェーンは80歳だが、今でも1年に300日近く旅をしている。彼女は、人々が他の人や動物、環境を助けるために持っている力について語っている。いつかあなたも、彼女に会って話をする機会があるかもしれない。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentences above?
問題01選択肢A: Although Jane is now eighty, she still spends nearly 300 days a year traveling, and she tells people that they themselves have the power to help others, animals, and nature; someday you might get the chance to meet her.
問題01選択肢B: Jane, who is eighty, travels almost 300 days a year to tell people about the power she has to help others, animals, and nature.
問題01選択肢C: Now that Jane is eighty, she no longer travels but instead talks to people about how they can help others, animals, and the environment.
問題01選択肢D: Because Jane is now eighty, she can travel only about 300 days a year, and she meets many people to talk with them.
問題01の解説: 原文は「80歳でも今なお300日近く旅をし、人々が(they)持つ力について語り、いつか会えるかもしれない」という意味。語彙・構造を変えつつ同義に述べたAが正解。Bは the power they have を the power she has に変え、力の持ち主を人々からジェーンにすり替えている(この一点で意味がずれる)。Cは she no longer travels(もう旅をしない)としており still travels と正反対。Dは逆接の but を理由の Because に変え、さらに only を加えて「年をとったので300日しか旅できない」と因果と数量を誤って伝えている。

問題: Some events of shock or great unhappiness often bring about phobias. If a little girl is bitten by a dog, she may be afraid of dogs even when she grows up. Maybe she knows not all the dogs will bite her, but she cannot get away from this fear.
訳: 衝撃的な出来事や大きな不幸は、しばしば恐怖症を引き起こす。幼い女の子が犬にかまれると、大人になっても犬を怖がるかもしれない。すべての犬が自分をかむわけではないとわかっていても、この恐怖から逃れることができないのだ。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the last sentence: "Maybe she knows not all the dogs will bite her, but she cannot get away from this fear."?
問題01選択肢A: She is certain that no dog will ever bite her, so she has completely lost her fear of dogs.
問題01選択肢B: Although she realizes that not every dog would bite her, she still cannot free herself from her fear.
問題01選択肢C: Because she believes that every dog will surely bite her, she is unable to overcome her fear.
問題01選択肢D: She understands that some dogs will not bite her, and this finally helps her get over her fear.
問題01の解説: 原文は『すべての犬がかむわけではない（部分否定）と知っていても、恐怖から逃れられない』という譲歩の内容なので、Bが同義です。Aは『no dog（全否定）』かつ『恐怖を失った』で意味が逆、Cは『every dog will bite（すべての犬がかむ）』と部分否定を取り違え、Dは前半は近いものの『恐怖を克服する』が原文の『逃れられない』と正反対になっています。

問題: Some languages in the long history of writing have "died" because there are no longer any native speakers or writers of the language. Such was the case with written "letters" called hieroglyphics: the meanings and the sounds of the hieroglyphic symbols had been lost over many centuries.
訳: 長い文字の歴史の中には、その言語を母語として話したり書いたりする人がもはやいないために「死んで」しまった言語もある。ヒエログリフと呼ばれる文字がまさにその例で、ヒエログリフの記号の意味と音は、何世紀もの間に失われてしまっていた。
問題01: Which one has the closest meaning to the sentences above?
問題01選択肢A: Some languages died out once no one was left to speak or write them naturally, and hieroglyphics is one whose symbols' meanings and sounds were lost over many centuries.
問題01選択肢B: Some languages lost all their native speakers and writers because those languages had already died, and hieroglyphics disappeared in the very same way.
問題01選択肢C: Hieroglyphics stopped being used, and although the sounds of its symbols were forgotten over the centuries, people have always kept knowing their meanings.
問題01選択肢D: Every language that people once wrote has died within a few years of losing its speakers, and hieroglyphics is the clearest example of this.
問題01の解説: The text says languages die *because* their native speakers and writers are gone, and that both the meanings and sounds of hieroglyphic symbols were lost over many centuries, which is exactly what A restates in reworded form. B reverses the cause and effect, C wrongly keeps the meanings known when the text says they were lost, and D changes "some" to "every" and "many centuries" to "a few years," so only A is truly synonymous.

問題: The Japanese language has throughout its history accepted with comparative ease many words from other languages.
訳: 日本語はその歴史を通じて、他の言語からの多くの語を比較的容易に受け入れてきた。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: Many other languages have, over their history, borrowed a large number of words from Japanese with relative ease.
問題01選択肢B: Throughout its history, Japanese has had great difficulty in taking in words from other languages.
問題01選択肢C: Over its history, Japanese has accepted only a few foreign words, and only with considerable effort.
問題01選択肢D: Over the course of its history, Japanese has taken in many words from other languages without much difficulty.
問題01の解説: 原文は「日本語が、その歴史を通じて、他言語からの多くの語を比較的容易に受け入れてきた」で、"with comparative ease" を without much difficulty と言い換えたDが同義。Aは借用の主客を逆にした誤り、Bは ease を difficulty に反転させた誤り、Cは数量(many→a few)と様態(容易→多大な努力)を逆にしている。

問題: In Australia, people called Aborigines regarded the rainbow snake as one of the creators of the earth.
訳: オーストラリアでは、アボリジニと呼ばれる人々は、虹の蛇を大地を創造したものの一つ(創造神の一柱)とみなしていた。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: In Australia, some people called the Aborigines together and viewed the rainbow snake as a creator of the earth.
問題01選択肢B: In Australia, the people known as Aborigines viewed the rainbow snake as one of the beings that had created the earth.
問題01選択肢C: In Australia, the people known as Aborigines viewed the rainbow snake as the one being that had created the whole earth.
問題01選択肢D: In Australia, the rainbow snake was thought by the Aborigines to be one of the earth's earliest inhabitants.
問題01の解説: 原文は「アボリジニと呼ばれる人々が、虹の蛇を大地を創った存在の一つとみなした」で、B が "people known as Aborigines" や「one of the beings that had created」と語彙・構造を変えつつ同義。A は "called" を述語動詞(呼び集めた)と誤読、C は "one of" を「唯一の創造者」に変えており、D は creators を inhabitants(住人)にすり替えて意味がずれている。

問題: The issue of obesity, rarely discussed before, has attracted more public attention because of the documentary film.
訳: 以前はめったに論じられることのなかった肥満の問題が、そのドキュメンタリー映画をきっかけに、より多くの世間の注目を集めるようになった。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: Obesity became such a widely discussed problem that someone finally produced a documentary film about it.
問題01選択肢B: Because obesity had often been debated in public, the documentary film about it attracted little notice.
問題01選択肢C: The documentary film seldom mentioned obesity, even though the public was paying close attention to it.
問題01選択肢D: The documentary film has drawn greater public attention to obesity, a problem that people had rarely talked about until then.
問題01の解説: Dは語彙と構造を変えつつ同義で、「映画が肥満への注目を高めた/その問題は以前はrarely talked about」という関係を正しく保っている。Aは因果が逆(問題が話題化→映画制作)。Bは "rarely" を "often" と逆にし、注目も減ったとする点で誤り。Cは "rarely" を「映画がめったに触れない」と主客・係り先を取り違えている。

問題: In order to promote his products, Sir Thomas Lipton had men dressed as Indians march through the city with placards.
訳: 自分の商品を宣伝するために、サー・トマス・リプトンは、インディアン(先住民)に扮した男たちに、プラカードを持って街じゅうを練り歩かせた。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: To advertise his goods, Sir Thomas Lipton dressed as an Indian and marched through the city carrying signs.
問題01選択肢B: To advertise his goods, Sir Thomas Lipton watched men in Indian costumes as they marched through the city with signs.
問題01選択肢C: To advertise his goods, Sir Thomas Lipton asked men to dress as Indians, but they refused to march through the city.
問題01選択肢D: To advertise his goods, Sir Thomas Lipton made men who were dressed as Indians walk through the city carrying signs.
問題01の解説: 使役の "had O do" は "made O do" で言い換えられ、"men dressed as Indians" は "men who were dressed as Indians" と同義なのでDが最も近い。Aは行進したのをリプトン自身にすり替えており誤り。Bは "had"(させた)を "watched"(見ていた)に変えて意味がずれ、Cは行進が実行されなかったと否定に転じており本文と矛盾する。

問題: You may have received a notice of acceptance to the university, but you will have to submit a number of documents before you can be officially admitted as a student.
訳: 大学から合格通知(入学許可の知らせ)を受け取っているかもしれないが、正式に学生として入学を認められるには、その前に多くの書類を提出しなければならないだろう。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: Once you send several documents to the university, you are sure to receive an acceptance notice and enroll as a student.
問題01選択肢B: You have certainly received an acceptance notice, so you no longer need to hand in any documents to enroll as a student.
問題01選択肢C: Even though you may already have an acceptance notice from the university, you will not be officially enrolled as a student until you submit many documents.
問題01選択肢D: You will receive an acceptance notice from the university only after you have submitted all the required documents.
問題01の解説: 原文は「合格通知は受け取っているかもしれない(可能性)が、正式な入学には多くの書類提出が必要」という内容で、Cがこれを正しく言い換えている。Aは書類提出を条件に合格通知が得られるとし因果を逆転。Bは "certainly"(確実に)と可能性を強め、さらに書類は不要と義務を否定している。Dは合格通知が書類提出の後に届くとして順序を取り違えており、いずれも意味がずれる。

問題: When I asked the college student if he could talk about Japanese literature he was at a loss for an answer.
訳: 私がその大学生に、日本文学について語れるかどうか尋ねると、彼は答えに窮してしまった。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: If the college student had been able to talk about Japanese literature, I would have asked him about it.
問題01選択肢B: When the college student asked me whether I could discuss Japanese literature, I could not answer him.
問題01選択肢C: When I asked the college student to talk about Japanese literature, he answered without any difficulty.
問題01選択肢D: When I asked the college student whether he could discuss Japanese literature, he did not know how to respond.
問題01の解説: 原文は「私が大学生に〜できるかどうか尋ねた」→「彼は答えに窮した」。Dは "whether he could discuss"(=if he could talk)と "did not know how to respond"(=was at a loss for an answer)で同義。Aは if を仮定法条件に読み替えており誤り。Bは尋ねた人と答えられなかった人を入れ替えている。Cは "answered without any difficulty" が原文と正反対。

問題: Whether you can get a good job or not depends on how well you can express yourself at a job interview.
訳: 良い仕事に就けるかどうかは、就職の面接でどれだけ上手に自分を表現できるかにかかっている。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: Whether or not you land a good job is determined by how effectively you can present yourself during a job interview.
問題01選択肢B: How well you present yourself at a job interview is determined by whether or not you land a good job.
問題01選択肢C: You can land a good job at an interview only when you avoid expressing your true self too openly.
問題01選択肢D: Even if you present yourself poorly at a job interview, whether you land a good job is purely a matter of luck.
問題01の解説: 原文は「良い仕事に就けるか」が「面接での自己表現のうまさ」に左右される、という構造で、A がそれを別語彙で正確に言い換えている。B は主語と決定要因を入れ替えた逆転。C は「表現を控えたときだけ職を得られる」と意味を反転させている。D は「運次第」という原文にない要素を加え、因果関係を消してしまっている。

問題: Whether at an elementary or high school level, one sign of a good teacher is whether he or she can find out a student who is in trouble and help that student get out of it.
訳: 小学校のレベルであれ高校のレベルであれ、良い教師である証の一つは、困っている生徒を見つけ出し、その生徒がそこ(困難)から抜け出す手助けができるかどうかということである。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: A good teacher, whether at an elementary or a high school, must choose whether to help a student in difficulty or to leave that student on his or her own.
問題01選択肢B: No matter whether the level is elementary or high school, one mark of a good teacher is being able to notice a student in difficulty and help that student escape from it.
問題01選択肢C: One sign of a good teacher is the ability to keep himself or herself out of difficulty, no matter whether he or she works at an elementary or a high school.
問題01選択肢D: Whether someone is a good teacher depends mainly on how many students in difficulty there are at the elementary or high school where he or she teaches.
問題01の解説: The original says that, regardless of the school level, a good teacher is marked by whether he or she can spot a troubled student and help that student out of the trouble; b keeps all of this. a wrongly adds the option of leaving the student alone. c misreads "a student who is in trouble" as the teacher's own trouble. d wrongly makes teaching quality depend on the number of struggling students rather than on the teacher's ability to help.

問題: For the first time in history, advances in science and technology have brought within reach what was once only a dream for hundreds of millions of people.
訳: 歴史上初めて、科学技術の進歩によって、かつて何億もの人々にとって単なる夢にすぎなかったものが、手の届くところにもたらされた。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: Thanks to progress in science and technology, something that used to be no more than a dream for huge numbers of people has, for the first time ever, become attainable.
問題01選択肢B: For the first time, hundreds of millions of people have begun to dream of what science and technology might someday achieve.
問題01選択肢C: Science and technology have advanced so far that what people once achieved has now become only a distant dream for many.
問題01選択肢D: Advances in science and technology have at last forced hundreds of millions of people to abandon a dream they had long cherished.
問題01の解説: 原文は「かつて夢でしかなかったものが手の届く範囲に来た=実現可能になった」の意で、"become attainable" と言い換えたAが同義。Bは「人々が科学技術の成果を夢見始めた」と主客・因果を逆転させている。Cは「実現していたことが夢になった」と方向を逆に、Dは「夢を捨てさせた」と正反対の内容で、いずれも意味が明確にずれる。

問題: Every author tries to convince us, their readers, that what they have to say is true and should be accepted as truth.
訳: どの著者も、読者である私たちに対して、自分の言いたいこと(言い分)は真実であり、真実として受け入れられるべきだ、と納得させようとするものだ。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: Each writer hopes that we, their readers, will decide whether what they say is really true and worth accepting.
問題01選択肢B: Each writer succeeds in persuading us, their readers, that everything they say is true and must be accepted as the truth.
問題01選択肢C: We readers try to persuade each writer that what we have to say is true and should be accepted as the truth.
問題01選択肢D: Each writer tries to make us, their readers, believe that their message is true and ought to be accepted as the truth.
問題01の解説: 原文の "tries to convince us ... that what they have to say is true and should be accepted as truth" は「著者が、自分の言い分は真実で真実として受け入れられるべきだと読者に納得させようとする」。Dは convince を make ... believe、should be accepted を ought to be accepted と言い換えつつ同義。Aは「納得させようとする」を「読者に真偽を判断してほしいと望む」に変えており意味がずれる。Bは tries を succeeds(成功する)に変え、さらに everything と過度に強めており誤り。Cは主語を著者から読者に入れ替えた主客逆転。

問題: At first I thought I was lucky to find a good place to see the parade. However, the woman behind whom I was sitting was wearing a big hat, so I could not see anything.
訳: 最初、私はパレードを見るのに良い場所を見つけられて運がいいと思った。しかし、私がその後ろに座っていた女性が大きな帽子をかぶっていたので、私は何も見ることができなかった。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to "the woman behind whom I was sitting was wearing a big hat, so I could not see anything"?
問題01選択肢A: A woman with a big hat was sitting behind me, so she blocked her own view of the parade.
問題01選択肢B: I was sitting behind a woman who was wearing a big hat, and it kept me from seeing anything.
問題01選択肢C: Though I sat behind a woman wearing a big hat, I could still see the whole parade well.
問題01選択肢D: The woman ahead of me removed her big hat, so I was finally able to see the parade.
問題01の解説: 原文は「私が後ろに座っていた(=前にいた)女性が大きな帽子をかぶっていて、私が何も見えなかった」の意で、Bがこれと一致する。Aは前後関係を逆にし見えなかった人物もすり替えており、Cは結果(見えなかった)を反対にし、Dは帽子を脱いで見えたという逆の内容になっている。

問題: What you see or hear is often defined by the character of the language through which you perceive it.
訳: あなたが見たり聞いたりするものは、あなたがそれを知覚する際に用いる言語の性質によって規定されることが多い。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: The language a person uses is often shaped by whatever that person happens to see or hear.
問題01選択肢B: Whatever a person sees or hears stays the same no matter which language is used to perceive it.
問題01選択肢C: What a person sees or hears is frequently shaped by the nature of the language used to perceive it.
問題01選択肢D: A person can see or hear things far more clearly by choosing a language of richer character.
問題01の解説: 原文は「見聞きするものが、それを知覚するのに用いる言語の性質によって規定される」の意で、"defined" を "shaped"、"the character" を "the nature" に言い換えたCが同義。Aは決定の方向を逆にしており、Bは "defined by" を否定して「言語に左右されない」と逆転、Dは本文にない「より鮮明に知覚できる」を加えている。

問題: The historical clues in the Bible lead researchers to a knowledge of the ancient civilizations in which the Bible was written.
訳: 聖書の中に残された歴史的な手がかりは、研究者たちを、その聖書が書かれた古代文明についての知識へと導いてくれる。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: Researchers discovered historical clues about when the Bible was written by first studying the ancient civilizations.
問題01選択肢B: Researchers must fully understand the ancient civilizations before they are able to find the historical clues in the Bible.
問題01選択肢C: By examining the historical clues found in the Bible, researchers can come to understand the ancient civilizations in which it was written.
問題01選択肢D: The historical clues in the Bible show researchers that the ancient civilizations produced many other written works.
問題01の解説: 原文は「聖書内の手がかりが研究者を、聖書が書かれた古代文明の知識へと導く」であり、C は studying clues → understand the civilizations という向きと内容を保った正しい言い換え。A は文明を調べて手がかりを得ると向きを逆転させ、B は文明の理解を手がかり発見の前提とし、D は「他の多くの著作を生んだ」という原文にない情報を加えており、いずれも意味がずれる。

問題: Advances in science of which we are proud have placed in the hands of our generation the power to destroy the whole of humankind.
訳: 私たちが誇りに思っている科学の進歩は、人類全体を滅ぼす力を私たちの世代の手に委ねることとなった。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: The power to wipe out the entire human race has made our generation proud of scientific progress.
問題01選択肢B: The scientific progress that we are proud of has protected our generation from anything that could wipe out the human race.
問題01選択肢C: Our generation, proud of scientific progress, has used its power to save the human race from destruction.
問題01選択肢D: The scientific progress that we are proud of has given our generation the power to wipe out the entire human race.
問題01の解説: 原文は「私たちが誇る科学の進歩が、人類全体を滅ぼす力を私たちの世代の手に与えた」という意味で、D が主語・動作・力の受け手のすべてで一致する。A は主語と目的語を逆にし「力が私たちを誇らせた」としている。B は "placed ... the power to destroy"(滅ぼす力を与えた)を "protected ... from"(〜から守った)と正反対にしている。C は "destroy" を "save from destruction"(破壊から救う)とねじ曲げている。

問題: The idea of girls attending school met strong opposition from adults in the village, where parents, unaware that urban societies encouraged girls' education and barely managing to survive, depended on their daughters to work.
訳: 少女が学校に通うという考えは、村の大人たちの強い反対にあった。その村では、都会の社会が女子教育を奨励していることを知らず、しかもかろうじて暮らしを立てている親たちが、娘たちを働き手として当てにしていたのである。
問題01: Which one is closest in meaning to the sentence above?
問題01選択肢A: The adults in the village encouraged girls to go to school, even though the parents knew that cities valued female education and could easily support themselves without their daughters' work.
問題01選択肢B: In the village, girls strongly objected to going to school, because their parents, who understood that cities promoted female education, forced them to work instead.
問題01選択肢C: In the village, adults strongly resisted letting girls attend school, since the parents there, ignorant that cities promoted female education and hardly able to make a living, needed their daughters to work.
問題01選択肢D: The adults in the village opposed girls' schooling, because the parents, aware that cities promoted female education but too poor to survive, still sent their daughters to work.
問題01の解説: 原文は「大人が反対（met strong opposition）」「親は都会が女子教育を奨励していると知らず（unaware）」「かろうじて生きていて（barely managing to survive）」「娘の労働を当てにしていた（depended on their daughters to work）」で、Cの resisted / ignorant / hardly able to make a living / needed their daughters to work がすべて対応する。Aは encouraged・knew・easily support と各要素を反対にしている。Bは反対したのを girls にし、親を understood としており主客と否定が誤り。Dは "aware"（知っていた）が "unaware" と逆で、"still sent their daughters to work" も就学させた含みが出て原意とずれる。
